title: The Way of Initiation, or How to Attain Knowledge of the Higher Worlds
author: Rudolf Steiner
description: The Way of Initiation, or How to Attain Knowledge of the Higher Worlds by Rudolf Steiner, in the early English translation by Max Gysi, with biographical notes on the author by Édouard Schuré (London: Theosophical Publishing Society, 1908), from the essays later published as Wie erlangt man Erkenntnisse der höheren Welten? Written while Steiner led the German Section of the Theosophical Society, it is a practical guide to spiritual development for modern people living in the world. It describes the conditions of esoteric training: reverence and devotion, inner tranquillity, meditation and the cultivation of moral qualities such as control of thought and action, equanimity and open-mindedness; and the stages of preparation, enlightenment and initiation, through which latent spiritual organs (the 'lotus flowers' or chakras) develop and the student meets the Guardian of the Threshold. It remains one of the most widely read introductions to Western meditative practice.
